headline: Baroness Campbell, a disabled member of the House of Lords, has delivered a speech in an AI-recreated version of her own voice, a first for the UK parliament.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a clear first for accessibility in a national parliament, confirmed by AFP and the Lords' own release, but small in scale.
importance_line: People who are losing their speech, and disabled lawmakers in particular, gain a precedent for being heard in their own voice with a parliament's approval, but it is one permission for one peer and the sources read do not say whether others could use it.
summary: AFP reports, as carried by The Economic Times, that Baroness Jane Campbell of Surbiton, an independent peer who has spinal muscular atrophy, a condition that worsens over time, used AI software to recreate her earlier voice and read out a speech she wrote herself during a health debate in the House of Lords on Tuesday. She had permission from the Lords' procedure committee and, AFP says, had approached ElevenLabs, a company that specialises in natural-sounding speech, to recreate the voice.
notes: The Times page (the pool source) returned no text, so the entry credits AFP, whose report was read on The Economic Times copy; the url is that copy. Tech Xplore and ITV pages were blocked. The Lords approval is also stated by a Vietnam.vn relay of the Lords announcement.
